speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This RCEP comprises 10 ASEAN members and the six dialogue partners with whom we have existing FTAs, that means, India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Some people have asked us if CPTPP and RCEP are two rival blocs or rival agreements.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As far as Singapore is concerned, these are complementary building blocks because what we envisage ultimately is a Free Trade Area of the Asia Pacific.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members would also know that we just signed an FTA with Sri Lanka last month.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There are some complexities involved with the EU-Singapore FTA that we are sorting out.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has been signed and it is just a question of ratification.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore is an associate member of the Pacific Alliance, which consists of Chile, Columbia, Mexico and Peru.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mercosur is also looking at exploring an FTA with Singapore as a step, ultimately, perhaps to a regional agreement between Mercosur and ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have been in this business long enough to know that when I used to go to South America 10 or 15 years ago, they were not interested in FTAs with us or with ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim asked about our immediate neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, let me report, first, Malaysia and Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We know these are our closest neighbours, of utmost importance.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And with the right spirit of cooperation, we embark on win-win initiatives, strengthen bilateral ties and allow our companies to tap on the dynamic Malaysian and Indonesian economies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But you know as well as I do, our relations will always be complex, and issues will surface from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When they do, again, have a sense of perspective.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Do not let a single issue derail the overall relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With Malaysia, we have continued to set new milestones recently.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The RTS Link, when completed in 2024, will dramatically change the way hundreds of thousands of travellers who shuttle between Johor Bahru and Singapore each day.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Then, we also have the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail which is also progressing well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The tender for the Assets Company was called last December.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The results of the tender will be announced in about a year's time and will be conducted in a fair, open and transparent manner.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Such long-term strategic projects enhance our interdependence, give us all a greater stake in each other's success and demonstrate the tangible benefits of stable and positive ties.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There have been questions even about Pedra Branca at the International Court of Justice.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will not let this issue define or derail our relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The most important point is this, that when we have a difference, we seek peaceful resolution according to international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I should say or should remind Members that Malaysia will soon hold its General Election.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Again, we know from past history that every time election rhetoric heats up, sometimes, Singapore becomes part of the political fodder.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On our part, we must ensure that we do not get drawn into their domestic politics, nor will we allow the import of foreign countries' politics into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With Indonesia, our bilateral cooperation remains deep and multifaceted.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Last year, Singapore and Indonesia commemorated "RISING50" – the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have been working to enhance economic linkages in digital economy, tourism and skills training.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are each other’s second biggest source of tourists.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The recently launched joint venture in Central Java, the Kendal Industrial Park, is doing well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Thirty-six companies have committed as tenants, with investments valued at over S$600 million, and with the potential to create 5,000 jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are also working with Indonesia on a digital industry cluster in Batam and to participate in the tech startup ecosystem in Jakarta which, by the way, has quite a thriving digital scene.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also continue to work closely to strengthen counterterrorism efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I just visited Jakarta last month, had a good series of meetings with my counterpart Ibu Retno Marsudi and other Indonesian leaders across the political spectrum.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is consensus across the board that the Singapore-Indonesia partnership is valuable and brings mutual benefits, and so long as we can continue this positive tenor, we can manage the inevitable differences which still remain.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Overall, we believe in the "Prosper Thy Neighbour" policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And this CIA is a unique long-standing arrangement that has brought economic benefits for both Brunei and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has lowered business costs and allowed us to interoperate.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee attended the Sultan's Golden Jubilee celebration last October, which is another occasion to reaffirm our close relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members may have heard that Brunei had a Cabinet reshuffle recently.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are familiar with many of the new Ministers because we have had regular exchanges over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we are looking forward to working with the new team to further take our special relationship to new heights.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We continue to foster close ties among the younger generation of Bruneian and Singapore leaders through the annual Young Leaders' Programme, led by His Royal Highness Crown Prince Billah and Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There were some questions on relationships with other key partners – Japan, Australia and India.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With Japan, our relations are close and multifaceted.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Last month, we hosted Foreign Minister Taro Kono.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam visited Japan in February, and the Prime Minister will be there in June.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are elevating cooperation in traditional sectors like trade and connectivity and also examining emerging areas like science and technology.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They have the Japan Society 5.0 vision which is very similar to our Smart Nation effort, and because of their lead with technology, we are looking at this as another platform for cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And both of us are ageing societies and that is another common challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will have to see how we can reorganise our societies and use technology to deal with this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull made an official visit in June 2017 for the 2nd Annual Leaders' Summit.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong will be going to Australia later this month.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: One point I would just highlight is that no other country provides as much space for us to train in as Australia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When you go there, it is multiple times the size of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang mentioned the emerging importance of India.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: India's population will exceed that of China, I think, by 2024.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: India hosted an ASEAN-India Commemorative Summit in New Delhi in January, which the Prime Minister attended.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have made good progress on the India-Singapore Strategic Partnership, particularly in smart cities and defence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to deliver the keynote address at the Shangri-La Dialogue in June this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We look forward to discussing ways to further expand our bilateral ties.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Senior Minister of State Mohamad Maliki will give Members more details.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we need to stay alert to known unknowns and unknown unknowns or "wild cards".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: How we in Singapore weather external shocks boils down to our domestic resilience and unity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think it was Mr Sitoh Yih Pin who asked about domestic support for foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So have the Members of Parliament (MPs) from the Workers' Party.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked about our public diplomacy efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members' questions are really centred on whether we can maintain domestic support and unity for our foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is why I said I am grateful that there is bipartisan support in this Chamber.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: International issues will increasingly be dragged into the domestic discourse.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our open, multiracial and multi-religious society gives many opportunities for foreign actors who are trying to test our resolve or even undermine our unity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans must be well-informed not only about the multitude and diversity of views but must also appreciate the corresponding tradeoffs that we have to weigh up.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans also have to be discerning towards "fake news" and not allow ourselves to be distracted and divided.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I wanted to quote our former President Dr Tony Tan at the S Rajaratnam Lecture last year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: He said that when someone sends you a message, take some time, reflect on the message, and ask yourself what it really means.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Think carefully about who stands to benefit from the proposed message and whether it is in Singapore's own national interest.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we do need strong and informed support from the public because foreign policy begins at home.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I also want to thank Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Cedric Foo for their questions on MFA officers and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think Members have noticed that MFA is the Ministry with the smallest budget.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is okay, I am not asking for more.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am actually very proud to have some of the most talented and dedicated officers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This includes even bringing in mid-career entrants with the relevant skillsets and experience.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And that is especially for our consular services, which, for most Singaporeans, is the public or human face of MFA.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We should bear in mind that this is a family enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What I have tried to do in my time there is to give credit and to emphasise family, and to tell my officers that they never need to be embarrassed about saying that they need to do something or that they need to take some time out because they need to address family needs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to seek the right balance, promote regional unity and pursue global economic opportunities wherever these arise.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will be honest, competent, reliable and constructive partners.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I will continue to work with all Members in this House to reach out to Singaporeans to build a deeper appreciation of the fundamental truths, the hard truths, that underpin our foreign policy, and to develop a shared national instinct against external attempts to pressure, influence or divide us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan spoke about Singapore’s main foreign policy priorities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will elaborate on Singapore’s relations with countries in the region and beyond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For good reasons, we place great importance on engaging our regional neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our future is inextricably linked to the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A peaceful and stable Southeast Asia is a necessary condition for Singapore’s security and prosperity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With 60% of ASEAN’s population under the age of 35, there are also demographic dividends to be reaped.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Therefore, we have pursued collaborative relations with our Southeast Asian neighbours, in particular, the provinces and regions outside the capitals of our two closest neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There are opportunities to deepen our engagement at the state and provincial levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have had visits by leaders from Sabah, Sarawak and Johor, as well as from Jambi, North Sumatra and Kepulauan Riau (KEPRI).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have visited places like Malacca, Perak, South Sumatra and West Java.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There is much unfamiliarity with Singapore in these places and vice-versa, especially among the youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is important to understand our neighbours at the local level and provide opportunities for them to know us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: What happens at the local level has an impact on their national politics and economies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some provincial leaders have also taken higher office at the national level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There are also potential economic opportunities in these states and regions for our businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Given our close proximity, Singapore cannot be immune.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, I have met pesantren students as well as undergraduates in Riau and Jambi.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The students were keen to discuss various topics, ranging from maintaining religious and racial harmony to the Singapore education system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both the students and I came away richer from having better understood each other’s perspectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked about our relations with other Southeast Asian countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We keep up regular high-level exchanges to deepen bilateral ties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last November, President Halimah Yacob attended the Royal Cremation Ceremony of His Majesty the late King Bhumibol Adulyadej of Thailand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong visited the Philippines and Vietnam twice last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Emeritus Senior Minister Goh Chok Tong and Minister Vivian Balakrishnan visited Myanmar, while Minister Vivian Balakrishnan also made introductory visits to the Philippines and Cambodia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hosted Laos Prime Minister Dr Thongloun Sisoulith as well as senior Vietnamese leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I also visited Brunei twice last year, including for Hari Raya Open Houses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have been doing this for several years now, and our friends from Brunei likewise visit Singapore during the Hari Raya season.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such interactions also provide opportunities for Singapore companies venturing into the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also in the process of negotiating a Bilateral Investment Treaty with Myanmar, which will give better protection for our companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While Southeast Asia remains the cornerstone of Singapore’s foreign policy, we should not lose sight of important regions elsewhere.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this globalised world, events elsewhere also affect Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will talk about three regions in particular – South Asia, Africa and the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In response to Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Murali Pillai, South Asia enjoys long-standing linkages to Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Politically, South Asia is an important part of the larger Indo-Pacific region which adjoins Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Economically, the region is driving growth in Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: South Asia's GDP is fast approaching US$3 trillion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our relationship with India remains broad-based and deep.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore is India’s 10th largest trading partner and second largest foreign investor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have made steady progress through the India-Singapore Strategic Partnership, particularly in skills development and smart cities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also worked with our economic agencies to support our companies’ expansion efforts in India.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, PSA inaugurated the Bharat Mumbai Container Terminals, which is now India’s largest container terminal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In keeping with India’s moves to digitalise its economy, we are also exploring new areas of cooperation, such as in financial technology (fintech).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: India’s technology startup scene is fast developing, with over 5,000 tech startups in 2017 alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singaporean startups, such as Anchanto, Shopmatic and ViSenze, are venturing into India to tap on its potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With the decentralisation of the government in India, we have actively engaged individual states, such as Maharashtra, to support Singapore’s business interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Following the State’s Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis’ visit to Singapore last year, a joint working group to share expertise and speed up investment proposals was proposed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also been supporting the development of Andhra Pradesh’s new capital city, Amaravati.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: India's Act East policy has put a spotlight on connecting the northeast of India to Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have launched a third skills centre in Guwahati, Assam, last year, after Delhi and Udaipur.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is Sri Lanka’s first modern and comprehensive FTA that not only highlights the economic opportunities but also provides savings for Singapore’s companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will visit us in a few weeks' time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will discuss economic cooperation and investments by Singapore and Bangladesh companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Africa is a vast continent of 54 countries that we cannot ignore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While many of us may be unfamiliar with Africa, Members would be surprised how many Africans know about Singaporeans and Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am constantly reminded during my trips to Africa of Singapore's reputation there, and the goodwill and trust that Africans have of us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many leaders from these countries have told me that they have all read founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew’s memoirs and want to learn more from us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Africa grows, we seek to position Singapore to take advantage of the economic opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Africa’s GDP is expected to reach US$3 trillion by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This year, we will host the 3rd High-Level Ministerial Exchange Visit from Africa, which will focus on how Singapore can partner Africa in smart city development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are working to put in place key economic frameworks, such as Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreements and Bilateral Investment Treaties, so that Singapore companies will find it easier to do business in Africa.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also making progress in aviation connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ethiopian Airlines relaunched flights to Addis Ababa, in addition to direct flights to Mauritius and South Africa.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Expanded air links will help boost business and tourism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about our engagement in the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It remains an important region for Singapore on several fronts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Economic reforms in many Middle East countries provide unprecedented opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 and National Transformation Programme 2020, hold bold and comprehensive reforms to diversify its economy from oil and to open up the country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our companies can tap on opportunities in areas, such as infrastructure development, healthcare and smart technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There is also good momentum in economic exchanges with UAE, our largest trading partner in the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A Singapore company, Rotary Engineering, won a contract to build 12 storage tanks for Dubai’s Emirates National Oil Company, increasing storage capacity by 50%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, the UAE Embassy in Singapore, the Singapore Business Federation and the Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce and Industry, set up the UAE-Singapore Business Council to link up companies and investors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our presence in the Middle East extends to North Africa and Central Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: My visit to Lebanon in May 2017 marked the first visit by a Singapore political officeholder to Lebanon since 1974.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We rekindled our ties with the Lebanese leadership and agreed to explore cooperation in areas of shared interests, such as counterterrorism and technical cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This year, I plan to bring a business delegation to Morocco to explore prospects for economic collaboration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the political level, I visited Iran last year and the Singapore Business Federation has mounted business missions to explore the Iranian market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For Central Asia, I met both the Mayors of Astana and Almaty during their visits to Singapore last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They had promising discussions with Singapore companies to explore economic ties with Kazakhstan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our people-to-people ties with the Middle East are strengthening.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The number of Singaporeans travelling to, living, studying or working in the Middle East is increasing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Wherever I have travelled, I have met many who have visited and spoke fondly of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our universities have many exchange programmes in the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over 500 students have participated in Singapore Management University's (SMU’s) Business Study Missions to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The National University of Singapore (NUS) Overseas College in Israel has also allowed many to experience Israel’s dynamic economic, business and entrepreneurship culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since 2007, NUS’ Middle East Institute has promoted a deeper understanding of the region by regularly inviting academics and experts from the Middle East for lectures and workshops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our engagements in the Middle East take place against the backdrop of a dynamic and complex region with rapid developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Events unfolding in the region reverberate across the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year alone, we saw the Gulf diplomatic crisis and the Israeli-Palestinian issue erupt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I had the opportunity to listen to different sides involved in the disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore respects their position and we do not take sides.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is our hope that all parties will be able to resolve their differences amicably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This has always been our approach, regardless of the vagaries of Middle East politics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan had explained in January 2018 Singapore’s vote in favour of the UN General Assembly resolution on the status of Jerusalem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We voted in favour of the resolution as it reaffirms previous UN resolutions, rejects any decisions or actions which purport to alter the character and status of Jerusalem, and calls for all States to comply with existing UNSC resolutions on Jerusalem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Before this, we had also voted in favour of UN General Assembly Resolution 37/123C in 1982, which deplored the relocation of diplomatic missions to Jerusalem, which was a violation of UNSC resolution 478 (1980).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The future status of Jerusalem should be decided through direct negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   The status of Jerusalem is a complex and sensitive issue with a long history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Any unilateral and premature action that might alter the status of Jerusalem will impede progress towards a just and durable solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The future status of Jerusalem should be decided through direct negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore has good relations with both the Israelis and Palestine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have urged both parties to resume direct negotiations and make progress towards a just and durable solution to the conflict.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Therefore, at the recent UN General Assembly, Singapore voted in support of the resolution to reject any decisions or actions that may change the nature or character of the status of Jerusalem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is consistent with Singapore’s vote in favour of UN General Assembly Resolution 37/123C in 1982, which deplored the relocation of diplomatic missions to Jerusalem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our long-standing view is that a two-state solution will help to bring peace and security to both parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore’s unwavering position on this issue has enabled us to be taken seriously and regarded as a friend who can be trusted and relied upon, and who can play a constructive role in international affairs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, our interests in the Middle East also stems from mutual interest to counter religious extremism together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I have just returned from Kuwait, where the Global Coalition to Defeat the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS) discussed how we can build on our successes and continue cooperating to eliminate terrorism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ultimately, our contributions towards the security and stability of the Middle East will help keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked how the SCP supports Singapore’s engagement of other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: SCP participants form a reservoir of goodwill and support for Singapore in international fora as well as their home countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Past SCP participants include Lao Prime Minister Dr Thongloun Sisoulith and several current leaders, ministers, mayors and governors of neighbouring countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: SCP gives us a useful platform to broaden our cooperation with other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have joint training partnerships with developed countries like the US and Japan, as well as developing countries like Thailand and Argentina, or countries in the region and beyond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Given the growing number of Singaporeans living and travelling overseas, Mr Ong Teng Koon’s question on their role in advocating for Singapore is timely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In today’s globalised and digitalised environment, foreign affairs are no longer the privileged purview of professional diplomats alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Increasingly, Singaporeans, especially those living abroad, play a role, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When overseas, our citizens may often be asked to explain Singapore’s policies and actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To do so effectively, an open mind and a friendly disposition help to bridge differences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We do not seek to impose our views on others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: By the same token, we must be conscious of who we are and defend what we stand for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are an independent, sovereign, multiracial country in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are not a Chinese, Indian or Malay state, and we must never act based on ethnic or religious identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When we deal with a foreign country, whether in business or social settings, we should stand firm against external pressures and influences that undermine our national identity, interests and values.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: How tall and strong Singapore stands in the international community depends on our own unity and cohesiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Whether our people are in Singapore or abroad should make no difference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now turn the floor over to Minister of State Sam Tan to continue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, MFA has been working closely with our economic agencies to create more opportunities for our people and businesses in Asia, Europe and Latin America.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I will elaborate on our efforts to strengthen Singapore’s connectivity to these partners and international organisations through diplomacy and trade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Statistics aside, Singaporeans can see and feel the growing economic ties with China.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: How are we managing this very important relationship in economics and beyond?

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, now please allow me to elaborate in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, 2018 marks the 40th anniversary of then-Senior Vice Premier Deng Xiaoping’s visit to Singapore in 1978.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is often said that "If you do not forget why you started, your mission can then be accomplished." Successive leaders have built upon the strong foundations laid by founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew and Deng Xiaoping to break new ground.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We have institutionalised frameworks that allow officeholders and officials to work together, address common challenges and seek new areas of cooperation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Beyond the three Government-to-Government projects, namely, the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park, Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City, and China-Singapore (Chongqing) Demonstration Initiative on Strategic Connectivity or Chongqing Connectivity Initiative, we also have seven business and economic councils with Guangdong, Jiangsu, Liaoning, Shandong, Sichuan, Tianjin and Zhejiang.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We also share many other links in multiple domains, such as culture, education, healthcare, technology and smart nation development, among others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is for this reason that both sides have described our relations as an "All-Round Cooperative Partnership Progressing with the Times".

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, the global economic landscape is expected to further transform in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As a centre for trade, transport, and finance, Singapore can partner different companies seeking to venture into Southeast Asia, China, India and other key markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Chongqing Connectivity Initiative-Southern Transport Corridor (CCI-STC) will shorten trade routes between western China and Southeast Asia and beyond to Europe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore is also well-placed to provide financial, legal and advisory services to support commercially viable B&R projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Several Chinese banks have already issued B&R bonds in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Confucius said: "Do not worry about not being known, just prove your worth." In other words, do not worry that you are unknown to others, so long as you have the real capability and are learned, other people will accept and appreciate you.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore's relevance to the world depends on our continued success and ability to innovate, adapt and improve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Many Chinese delegations have visited Singapore on study trips and attended courses over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are an interesting case study to the Chinese and other partners, not only because we share good relations, but also because of our pragmatic and time-tested approaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: However, it is not a one way traffic; we are learning from each other and working together for mutual benefit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Today, both sides continue to exchange views through high-level platforms, such as JCBC, the Singapore-China Social Governance Forum, the Singapore-China Forum on Leadership and the Singapore-China Legal and Judicial Roundtable, and so on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Going forward, for Singapore to thrive in the global arena, we have to be resourceful, firmly uphold international law, and do so in a respectful but not submissive manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: If Singapore is to continue playing a constructive international role and protect our interests, we should strive to punch above our weight, expand our international space and create more opportunities for Singaporeans to broaden our horizons and establish our global presence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, now allow me to continue in English.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As we push on with our Smart Nation vision, we can learn from others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Cedric Foo sought an update on our cooperation with Japan and the ROK.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As mentioned by Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, Japan's "Society 5.0" initiative broadly converges with our Smart Nation priorities by leveraging technology and innovation to advance its economy and also to resolve social issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are also keen to develop a partnership with the ROK on innovation and smart cities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Henry Kwek had requested for an update on our relations with Europe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: While the impact of Brexit unfolds, Europe continues to be a key market and valuable partner in innovation, education and skills development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, we are partnering France to expand into industries of the future, such as Fintech, Smart Cities and Emerging Technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In a climate of increased protectionism, we support our European partners' strong commitment to free trade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: While we work towards ratifying the EU-Singapore FTA, we have also begun negotiating the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU)-Singapore FTA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I am also happy to report that the Singapore-Turkey FTA came into effect last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: With increased connectivity, Singapore will stand to gain from increased investment, tourism, trade and employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Further afield, Singapore is an Observer in the Arctic Council.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Melting ice caps and new Arctic sea routes present both challenges and opportunities for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Shipping traffic could be diverted in the long run, but Singapore companies could leverage the emerging sectors in the Arctic, such as shipbuilding and repair, port management and offshore engineering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about our engagement of emerging markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Although the world appears more integrated than before, we cannot take the status quo for granted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As a small state grappling with forces beyond our control, Singapore must strongly support a rules-based multilateral order underpinned by international law, a point that was emphasised by Minister Vivian Balakrishnan earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about our role in the international community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: At the UN, Singapore will continue to uphold our reputation as a principled, responsible and reliable country and partner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In July this year, we will attend a High Level Political Forum in New York to share our developmental experience in relation to the Sustainable Development Goals under the 2030 Agenda.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will continue to participate in negotiations on the implementation guidelines of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Comprising 20 major economies that account for 85% of the world GDP and two-thirds of its population, the G20 makes decisions that affect the rest of us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is, therefore, important and also an honour for Singapore to participate in the G20 to offer our perspective and contribute where we can.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Consular assistance for overseas Singaporeans remains one of MFA's more visible core functions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Last year, 2017, was a very busy year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We responded to a number of overseas incidents, including multiple attacks and natural disasters at tourist hotspots.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, when Mount Agung erupted in December last year, our crisis response team was on the ground to help Singaporeans affected by airport closures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We also assisted Singaporeans who were involved in road traffic accidents in the US, Australia and, closer to home, in Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will continue to do our best to assist Singaporeans who are caught in difficult situations overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: However, we also urge our fellow Singaporeans to continue to practise personal responsibility and self-reliance and vigilance as our MFA staff are not able to be everywhere all the time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: So, in this regard, I was heartened that many Singaporeans travelled to Johor on their own to join in the search-and-rescue efforts for our two missing hikers in Mount Pulai recently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Likewise, local Singaporean communities abroad are often the first line of support and assistance for one another, and also to fellow Singaporeans travelling to that part of the world, especially when the nearest MFA representation is far away.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And on our part, MFA will endeavour to provide useful and timely information to Singaporean travellers through technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, we provide country-specific travel information on our revamped MFA website and are working with Government agencies and relevant partners to broaden our reach via various platforms, such as AskJamie@MFA, Chatbot and the Singapore Airport Terminal Services (SATS) travel application.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: However, given the free flow of information and disinformation, we hope that Singaporeans will continue to be vigilant and discerning and not to take information at face value.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This will prevent a repeat of the false reports about riots in Batam last year that caused a lot of unnecessary alarm and anxiety to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We do have just a few more minutes for clarifications.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But let me just focus on one point that the Minister flagged out.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: And that was the threat of fake news.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is our regulatory and our enforcement approach.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, as I said, we do not have a say, but we will comply with all UNSC Resolutions.
